SubscribeSign inProspectusRobotics will Evolve with Generative AI 

Google DeepMind robotics papers, but something even more surprising out of Stanford. 

Michael SpencerJan 08, 2024∙ Paid6295Share

Hey Everyone, 

As we head into 2024, it’s not just Generative A.I. that is in a secular research boom, it’s the field of robotics as well. 

What’s interesting to me is a lot of this is also occurring under the radar of most media coverage. As stunning as advancements were in 2023 with Generative A.I., don’t sleep on robotics going more mainstream in the next few years. 

Robots at Amazon

Michael Spencer and Conrad Gray·November 23, 2023Hey Everyone, In 2023 I’ve become increasingly interested in robots and the advent of robotics in mainstream society. Conrad Gray has been helping me with this coverage a lot. For example, Amazon has grown up to be a huge employer in the United States and some other countries. As of September, 2023 the U.S. e-commerce multinational headquartered in Seat…

Read full storyThis post by Conrad Gray of Humanity Redefined Newsletter. 

A few days ago Google DeepMind, launched three new papers for advanced robotics that show how we can help robots make faster decisions, and better understand and navigate their environments.

The first, AutoRT, brings together large vision and language models with robotic control models in a single system, which could help create robots that understand practical human goals in much more natural ways. The resulting system safely orchestrated as many as 20 robots simultaneously, gathering a diverse dataset across 6,650 unique tasks.

The other two papers present a new system for scaling up the efficiency and speed of Robotic Transformers (SARA-RT), and a system for improving the generalization of learning robotic motions by sketching trajectories over top training videos (RT-Trajectory).
